sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.id, c.name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
SELECT DISTINCT id, name FROM customer
SELECT id, name FROM customer GROUP BY id, name
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING customer_id > 2
SELECT c.id, o.status FROM customer c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'paid'
SELECT DISTINCT c.id, c.name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id ORDER BY c.id DESC
SELECT DISTINCT c.id, c.name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id ORDER BY c.id LIMIT 3 OFFSET 1
SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id ORDER BY c.name
SELECT DISTINCT c.id, c.name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'paid' OR o.status IS NULL
SELECT DISTINCT c.id, c.name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE UPPER(o.status) = 'PAID'
SELECT DISTINCT c.id, c.name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'paid'
SELECT DISTINCT c.id, UPPER(c.name) AS display_name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
SELECT DISTINCT UPPER(c.name) AS display_name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
SELECT DISTINCT c.id, c.name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id > c.id
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING customer_id > 2 AND COUNT(*) > 1
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING customer_id IS NOT NULL AND COUNT(*) > 1
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING (customer_id = 1 OR customer_id = 2) AND COUNT(*) > 1
SELECT c.id, o.status FROM customer c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING customer_id > 2 OR COUNT(*) > 1
SELECT DISTINCT c.id, o.status FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
SELECT id, name FROM customer WHERE name = NULL
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
SELECT id, name FROM customer WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)
